cohort: 600 singleton pregnant women in 15-28 weeks of pregnancy
finding: Thyroid autoimmunity, even without thyroid dysfunction, is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preeclampsia, preterm delivery, IUGR, and low Apgar scores, suggesting the need for further investigation into screening and treatment during pregnancy.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was significantly higher in mothers with abnormal TSH and positive anti-Tg antibodies.
